newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian ADRs set to grow this year - Salomon Bros.
newsitem.headline: Russian ADRs set to grow this year - Salomon Bros.

text.p: American Depositary Receipts in leading Russian companies have so far this year outperformed several leading indices, and ADRs will continue to appreciate, investment bank Salomon Brothers said.

"So far in 1997, a market-cap weighted portfolio of Russian ADRs would have achieved a 28 percent return; a similar portfolio excluding Gazprom ADRs would have earned 54 percent," it said in a report dated May 14.
"Six of the nine ADRs outperformed the global emerging market indices," it said.
Salomon projected ADR market capitalisation would grow from $4.6 billion currently, or seven percent of the Russian market's total capitalisation, to $8-$10 billion by the end of the year.
ADRs will particularly benefit from new flows of funds into Russian equities, the report said.
"ADRs are well positioned to benefit from a liquidity-driven market for the rest of 1997... We anticipate rising demand for Russian exposure driving Russian ADR prices up to new highs," it said.

Plans of four companies with level-one ADRs, which allow existing shares to be traded abroad, to issue new capital through level-three receipts could help boost prices for current ADRs in those firms.
LUKoil, Mosenergo, Tatneft and Chernogorneft have said they are looking at issuing level-three ADRs.

Local shares in some companies preparing to issue their first ADRs also showed potential for appreciation in the run-up to the issue, the report said, tipping regional telecoms and national power company UES as promising buys in the next few months.
